content.comment_body: Previously, there was an Excel spreadsheet shared on this and the German forum that allowed users to access a [product_name] to read and set values, communicating via the serial port. However, newer PCs and [product_name] models no longer have serial ports. Has anyone updated this Excel tool to work over Ethernet for the latest [product_name]?
I am not aware of any such update.
It's unfortunate, since the Excel method was very effective for system setup. Entering values in a spreadsheet and loading them into the [product_name] made the process straightforward.

[user_name], In my situation, I made all parameter adjustments using the built-in screen, running a simulation and then transferring the updated program to the [product_name]. The newer [product_name] includes a web server that replicates the screens on a web page, allowing for private pages where adjustments can be made. This means anyone with a web-enabled device and login can adjust parameters without special software. Additionally, there is a mobile app you can try—search Google Play for more information. Does this help? [user_name]

Using Excel was helpful for sanity-checking values before configuring the [product_name]. Users would fill in the required values in the spreadsheet for the specific machine or process run, and simple logic checks in Excel could catch errors—like preventing someone from entering -300°C for a process temperature.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants desire a seamless way to configure and verify parameters on the [product_name], especially for newer models, using Excel. While the previous serial-based solution is no longer viable, there is a clear preference for spreadsheet-driven validation and upload via Ethernet, rather than relying solely on web server or mobile app solutions, which may not offer pre-configuration error checking.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to continue using Excel to easily enter, validate, and transfer configuration settings to the latest [product_name] models over Ethernet, similar to how the process worked previously with serial communication.
pain_keywords: lack of Ethernet support for Excel workflow
